A suspension is not an immediate action and will take place on the plan's upcoming monthly renewal date
[banana365] When I checked after they changed the subscription model, you need to pay the activation fee each time you "unpause" it. In other words, if you go on two trips a year you have to pay 2x$70 plus the subscription fee. This was confirmed at the time by Garmin. So it's definitely not a lot cheaper for many usage types compared to the previous model. The price went up significantly for my usage. I've now just let the subscription lapse totally (this was for one of the mapping GPS inreach units, so still a useful device).
Given the availability of mobile phone to LEO satellite comms these days, I think Garmin are just trying to get as much cash as they can for this product division before it totally loses its differentiator.
[Banj0] Yeah, I turn mine off and on as required. Also, I go for a slightly higher plan if it’s multi day and my family can track me a little better.

Is an acceptable subscription model. For sure, if you suspend it won’t take place until the paid month ends. Having to activate it only one month after twelve is fine.

[eug] What's with the micro-USB charging port? How old is this device?
Satellite comms equipment (apart from Starlink) have very long product lifecycles. They do not follow the typical consumer product lifecycle where companies release a new model every year with barely any changes. They are serious devices that focus on reliability rather than novelty, so if a design works well, it is kept for a very long time.
e.g. the current industry-standard Iridium satellite phones are the Iridium 9555 and 9575 Extreme which were released in 2008 and 2011. The 9575 uses a mini USB port on a dongle which plugs in to the bottom of the phone.
The 9555 never had a USB port, it uses a tiny DC plug. They did just release an updated model of the same phone (with monochrome LCD intact) and a Type-C socket last month though.

[OZKap] If you don't need the messaging features a Personal Locator Beacon is cheaper and doesn't need a subscription to operate.
[eug] The two devices are for different uses. If someone only needs a device that sends a "I am going to die, send help" message, a PLB is perfect. No one who only needs that would even consider a device like this.
This device is for people who, instead of calling for a full emergency response, might want to ask the emergency response team "I've [insert injury here], I can stay overnight if the weather is OK, what is the forecast?"
Or "My 4WD has a mechanical failure, I have 2 days food and water, I don't need emergency services but I need a mechanic".
The automated live tracking feature is also useful for giving friends and family peace of mind. If someone is running late they can give progress updates, and if a person is no longer able to respond or is unable to activate a PLB at least they can be located.
[OZKap] If someone only needs a device that sends a "I am going to die, send help" message, a PLB is perfect.
Generally we prefer if people signal before it gets that dire, but sure.
Just letting people know that there are options available. I doubt the average Ozbargain user is a survival aficionado.
The automated tracking features do sound nice. Personally I'd rather rely on the worldwide SAR capabilities of the PLB/EPIRB system than a private company but I haven't hugely looked into Garmin

[ProlapsedHeinous] @Cheap Gamer: With garmin you have the option of urgent but not life critical (normal sms) or you can press the emergency button and text with emergency service call centre who will relay the info. you can tell the emergency team whats wrong exactly, perhaps before you are in a situation where you can no longer communicate. Then when rescue arrives, they already know what might be wrong and can go to work on the previously supplied info. otherwise with an epirb the rescue team will come out and may not have the tools for whatever situation you are in. If you have a week of food and water and all you need is a tow, that is going to prevent a lot of people risking their own lives to come and rescue you. All they will do is rock up, hand you a satellite phone and wait while you book a tow truck. thats a complete waste of resources all because you don't want to spend 40 bucks a month for shtf peace of mind.
